pairing_hello.name: computer-name
pairing_hello.rule: a computer names itself "OS - Hostname" (section 4.3 item 3)

pairing_hello.name: computer-name-non-ascii
pairing_hello.rule: the name is UTF-8; the bound counts bytes (section 7.1)

pairing_hello.name: phone-name
pairing_hello.rule: an iPhone or iPad sends its own or its model name, which already says the platform, without an operating-system prefix (section 4.3 item 3)

pairing_hello.name: tablet-name
pairing_hello.rule: an iPad is a requester and sends its model name without a prefix (section 4.3 item 3)

pairing_hello.name: android-tablet-name
pairing_hello.rule: an Android tablet's name does not say the platform, so it carries the prefix (section 4.3 item 3)

pairing_hello.name: name-over-bound
pairing_hello.rule: a name over 256 bytes is a protocol violation; a sender shortens its name to fit (section 7.1)

pairing_hello.name: name-empty
pairing_hello.rule: an empty name is a protocol violation (section 7.1)

pairing_hello.name: name-blank
pairing_hello.rule: a name of white space alone is a protocol violation (section 7.1)

session_name.name: ready-same-name
session_name.rule: the custodian's name in session.ready equals the record's; nothing is rewritten (section 4.3 item 4)

session_name.name: ready-renamed
session_name.rule: a renamed phone's new name replaces the record's (section 4.3 item 4)

session_name.name: ready-name-missing
session_name.rule: session.ready without display_name is an authenticated protocol violation; the record keeps its name (section 7.1)

session_name.name: ready-name-blank
session_name.rule: a blank name closes the session; the record keeps its name (section 4.3 item 4)

session_name.name: hello-same-name
session_name.rule: the requester's name in session.hello equals the record's (section 4.3 item 4)

session_name.name: hello-renamed
session_name.rule: a renamed computer's new name replaces the record's (section 4.3 item 4)

session_name.name: hello-name-over-bound
session_name.rule: a name over 256 bytes closes the session; the record keeps its name (section 7.1)

session_name.name: hello-name-missing
session_name.rule: session.hello without display_name is an authenticated protocol violation (section 7.1)
